title: Game/entire PC display driver crashing on specific AMD hardware
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6, 4.6.1, 4.7, 4.7.1
- Unable to test previous versions due to project requirements

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 535.309.01) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.26 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

**Disclaimer**: The system information is mine. The following is the tester in question's:
OS: Windows 11
CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700K CPU @ 3.80GHz
RAM: 16 GB
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 5600 XT
Renderer: Issue occurs on both Vulkan and D3D12 (Forward+)

One of my testers has been having their game crash in a 3D environment after a certain period of time, ranging anywhere from 30 seconds to 12 minutes. The 3D environment in question is a relatively basic flat plane with some cuboid meshes with "PSX-styled" building meshes on top, + a mountain mesh in the background made through a displacement shader.

Initially, when the game ran on Vulkan on Windows, it gave the following error:

```ERROR: ** Report from VK_EXT_device_fault **
Description: No fault detected
Vendor infos:
Addresses info:
   at: on_device_lost (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:6993)
ERROR: === Driver Memory Report ===
Launch with --extra-gpu-memory-tracking and build with DEBUG_ENABLED for this functionality to work.
Device memory may be unavailable if the API does not support it(e.g. VK_EXT_device_memory_report is unsupported).

Total Driver Memory:0.0 MB
Total Driver Num Allocations: 0
Total Device Memory:0.0 MB
Total Device Num Allocations: 0

Memory use by object type (CSV format):

Category; Driver memory in MB; Driver Allocation Count; Device memory in MB; Device Allocation Count
   at: on_device_lost (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:7002)
ERROR: Vulkan device was lost. This could be due to a driver issue, a hardware issue, or the driver resetting itself because it was unresponsive for too long (TDR).
   at: command_queue_execute_and_present (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:3268)
```

Attempting to run a debug build with the `--extra-gpu-memory-tracking` argument just caused this entire block to be replaced with "Illegal instruction" in the output.

Someone suggested I switch the game to use D3D12 on windows. This did not fix the issue, but it caused a much
[much more verbose error log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31281281/godot.2.log).

It seems that something is causing the GPU to "reject' or disconnect from the game/PC, but I am unsure what.

This report also seems highly related, suggested it might be a bug exclusive to RDNA1's architercture:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/121402

A quick search says that these are RDNA1 GPUs:

RX 5700 XT (Navi 10 - High performance, 8GB GDDR6)
RX 5700 (Navi 10 - Mid-high performance, 8GB GDDR6)
RX 5600 XT / RX 5600 (Navi 10 - Mid-range, 6GB GDDR6)
RX 5500 XT / RX 5500 (Navi 14 - Budget, 4GB/8GB GDDR6)
RX 5300 / RX 5300 XT (Navi 14 - Entry-level/OEM)
Radeon RX 5600M and RX 5500M (Laptop variants)

### Steps to reproduce

Unfortunately, I do not have frequent enough access to this tester/their hardware to be able to tell what exactly causes the issue. The related issue I linked above has a reproduction project attached. I have also attached the scene below.

Here is a version of the scene decoupled from the game.
